title: Database Management Systems
subject: core-cs
description: An in-depth study of relational database systems, covering data modelling, SQL, normalization, query processing, transactions, concurrency control, indexing and crash recovery. Students learn both how to design and query databases and how a DBMS executes and protects those queries internally.

units.title: Unit 1 · Relational Model and SQL
units.description: The relational data model, keys and ER-based conceptual design, followed by the SQL language for defining and querying data.

topics.title: Relational Model and ER Modelling
topics.description: Relations, tuples and attributes, super/candidate/primary/foreign keys, ER diagrams and mapping ER designs to tables.

documents.title: Relational Model and ER Modelling — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Relational terminology, the hierarchy of keys with examples, ER constructs and cardinality, and rules for mapping ER diagrams to SQL tables.

topics.title: SQL Fundamentals
topics.description: DDL and DML, the SELECT-FROM-WHERE block, joins, grouping, subqueries and NULL semantics, with hands-on query practice.

documents.title: SQL Fundamentals — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Logical evaluation order of a query, inner and outer joins on example tables, GROUP BY and HAVING, three-valued logic and subqueries.

documents.title: SQL Practice: Worked Query Examples
documents.description: Lab handout with a Student/Course/Enrollment schema, sample data and eight solved queries with their exact results.

units.title: Unit 2 · Database Design and Query Processing
units.description: Schema refinement using functional dependencies and normal forms, and the algebra and algorithms a DBMS uses to evaluate queries.

topics.title: Functional Dependencies and Normal Forms
topics.description: Anomalies, functional dependencies, Armstrong's axioms, attribute closure, 1NF through BCNF, lossless join and dependency preservation.

documents.title: Functional Dependencies and Normal Forms — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Closure computation, normal form definitions, a step-by-step decomposition to BCNF and the 3NF versus BCNF trade-off.

topics.title: Relational Algebra and Query Processing
topics.description: Relational algebra operators, query trees, heuristic and cost-based optimization, and the I/O cost of join algorithms.

documents.title: Relational Algebra and Query Optimization — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Selection, projection, set operators, joins and division, translation of SQL to query trees and equivalence-based rewriting.

documents.title: Join Algorithms and I/O Cost — Reference Sheet
documents.description: Cost formulas for nested-loop, block nested-loop, index nested-loop, sort-merge and hash joins with a fully computed example.

units.title: Unit 3 · Transactions, Concurrency and Storage
units.description: Transaction semantics and concurrency control, followed by physical storage, index structures and crash recovery.

topics.title: Transactions and Concurrency Control
topics.description: ACID properties, schedules and serializability, two-phase locking, deadlock handling and SQL isolation levels.

documents.title: Transactions, Schedules and Serializability — Lecture Notes
documents.description: ACID explained with a bank transfer, concurrency anomalies, conflict serializability via precedence graphs and recoverable schedules.

documents.title: Locking, Deadlocks and Isolation Levels
documents.description: Shared and exclusive locks, 2PL and its strict variants, wait-die and wound-wait, the isolation level anomaly table and MVCC.

topics.title: Indexing, Storage and Recovery
topics.description: Pages and files, clustered and secondary indexes, B+ trees and hash indexes, write-ahead logging and the ARIES recovery algorithm.

documents.title: Storage, Indexing and B+ Trees — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Page-based storage, clustered versus non-clustered index costs, B+ tree fan-out, splits and merges, and hash indexes.

documents.title: Logging and Crash Recovery: WAL and ARIES
documents.description: Steal/no-force policies, the WAL rules, fuzzy checkpoints and a traced run of the ARIES analysis, redo and undo phases.
